items.def: to examine something carefully in order to understand it or explain how its parts work
items.ex: Researchers analysed the survey responses to find out why so many students prefer recorded lectures.

items.def: to judge the size, quality, value or importance of something after thinking about it carefully
items.ex: Before launching the scheme, the company assessed its likely impact on staff who work from home.

items.def: to show that something is true, exists or is likely to happen
items.ex: The figures indicate that demand for evening courses rose steadily between 2015 and 2020.

items.def: to show or explain something, especially by using a chart, picture or example
items.ex: The bar chart illustrates how many hours employees in four countries spent commuting each week.

items.def: a part or share of a whole, often given as a percentage or fraction
items.ex: The proportion of adults who read the news on their phones doubled over the decade.

items.def: close to a particular number or amount, but not exactly
items.ex: Approximately two thirds of the respondents said they used public transport to get to work.

items.def: in the same order as the things you have just mentioned
items.ex: Spending on research and on marketing reached 12% and 18% of the budget respectively in 2020.

items.def: when everything is considered; used to introduce a general summary
items.ex: Overall, the number of people working from home increased, while office attendance fell.

items.def: to change often, rising and falling in an irregular way
items.ex: Sales of laptops fluctuated between two and three million units before rising sharply in 2020.

items.def: to become smaller, weaker or less in number or quality; a fall of this kind
items.ex: Newspaper sales declined steadily over the period, while online subscriptions grew rapidly.

items.def: to reach the highest point or level; the highest point
items.ex: Home internet use peaked at 9 pm and then fell steadily until the early morning.

items.def: large in amount, size, value or importance
items.ex: Training staff to use the new software required a substantial amount of time.

items.def: used to compare two facts and show how they are different
items.ex: Younger employees preferred flexible hours, whereas older staff valued job security more highly.
items.fam: no derived forms; compare while, whilst (conj)

items.def: as a result of what has just been mentioned
items.ex: Many firms moved their training online; consequently, their travel costs fell significantly.

items.def: to form a particular part or amount of something; also, to explain why something happens
items.ex: Smartphones accounted for nearly half of all online purchases in the final year shown.

items.def: facts, signs or information that show whether something is true
items.ex: There is growing evidence that regular exercise improves concentration at work.

items.def: gas, heat or another substance sent out into the air, especially by vehicles and factories
items.ex: Allowing staff to work from home two days a week could cut the carbon emissions caused by commuting.

items.def: able to continue for a long time without damaging the environment or using up natural resources
items.ex: Universities are under pressure to adopt more sustainable practices, such as reducing paper use.

items.def: an idea that might explain something but has not yet been proved, used as a starting point for research
items.ex: The researchers tested the hypothesis that shorter meetings would help employees make better decisions.

items.def: to consist of particular parts or members; to be made up of
items.ex: The research team comprised three engineers, two designers and a data analyst.

items.def: extremely important, because it affects what happens next
items.ex: Clear communication is crucial when team members work in different time zones.

items.def: having a good or helpful effect
items.ex: Short breaks away from screens are beneficial for both concentration and eyesight.

items.def: causing harm or damage
items.ex: Spending long hours on social media late at night can have a detrimental effect on students' sleep.

items.def: negative and harmful; not good for someone or something
items.ex: Some parents worry that violent video games may have adverse effects on children's behaviour.

items.def: certain to happen and impossible to avoid or prevent
items.ex: As machines take over routine tasks, some changes to the way we work seem inevitable.

items.def: important or interesting enough to deserve attention
items.ex: The most notable change was the sharp fall in the number of households with a landline phone.

items.def: (of energy) coming from sources that are naturally replaced, such as wind, sunlight or moving water
items.ex: Several technology companies now aim to power their data centres entirely with renewable energy.

items.def: a factor that can change in an experiment or situation and may affect the result
items.ex: The study controlled for other variables, such as age and income, before comparing the two groups.

items.def: to show that something is especially important or deserves special attention
items.ex: The report emphasises the need for better digital skills among older workers.

items.def: to give a good reason for a decision or action
items.ex: It is hard to justify spending so much on new equipment when many classrooms need basic repairs.

items.def: to accept or admit that something is true or exists
items.ex: Although I acknowledge that online courses are convenient, I believe face-to-face teaching is more effective.

items.def: to be greater or more important than something else
items.ex: In my view, the benefits of flexible working far outweigh the drawbacks.

items.def: the information or conclusions that a study or investigation discovers
items.ex: The findings suggest that students who get more sleep tend to achieve higher grades.

items.def: the natural place where a particular animal or plant usually lives
items.ex: The construction of new roads has destroyed the habitats of many local bird species.

items.def: a particular way of thinking about something, often shaped by your situation or experience
items.ex: From an employer's perspective, remote work can significantly lower the cost of office space.
items.fam: no common derived forms; similar: viewpoint, standpoint

items.def: something you believe is true although you have no proof
items.ex: Many people make the assumption that young people are naturally good with technology.

items.def: the final result of an action, process or event
items.ex: The outcome of the six-month trial was a permanent four-day working week for all staff.
items.fam: no common derived forms; similar: result

items.def: a possible effect or result of an action or decision, which may not be obvious at first
items.ex: The rise of artificial intelligence has serious implications for the way schools assess students.

items.def: to organise and carry out an activity such as research, a survey or an experiment
items.ex: The researchers conducted a survey of 500 office workers about their screen habits.

items.def: all the living things in an area and the way they affect each other and their surroundings
items.ex: Plastic waste in the sea threatens the delicate ecosystems of coral reefs.

items.def: to improve the quality, value or strength of something
items.ex: Interactive whiteboards can enhance students' engagement during lessons.

items.def: to make a determined effort to deal with a difficult problem
items.ex: Governments must work together to tackle the growing problem of electronic waste.

items.def: to start dealing with a problem or question
items.ex: The new policy fails to address the shortage of qualified science teachers.

items.def: to decide which things are most important and deal with them first
items.ex: Schools should prioritise practical skills over the memorisation of facts.

items.def: to examine a situation or problem carefully in order to discover the truth about it
items.ex: Scientists are investigating whether light from screens affects the quality of our sleep.

items.def: to protect something from harm or loss, or to use it carefully so that it lasts longer
items.ex: Offices can conserve energy by switching off computers and lights at night.

items.def: a disadvantage or problem that makes something less attractive
items.ex: The main drawback of online meetings is that it is harder to build personal relationships.
items.fam: no derived forms; similar: disadvantage, downside

items.def: based on good reasoning or evidence and therefore reasonable to accept
items.ex: Critics make a valid point when they say that screen time is difficult to measure accurately.

items.def: including everything or almost everything that is needed or relevant
items.ex: The company offers a comprehensive training programme for all new employees.

items.def: causing a lot of public disagreement or strong argument
items.ex: The use of facial recognition cameras in schools remains highly controversial.

items.def: a small group of people or things chosen from a larger group in order to test or study it
items.ex: The survey used a sample of 1,200 university students from three different countries.

items.def: a substance that makes air, water or soil dirty and harmful
items.ex: Old diesel buses release pollutants that harm the health of people living near busy roads.

items.def: existing or happening in many places or among many people
items.ex: The widespread use of smartphones has changed the way people search for information.

items.def: forming the basic and most important part of something
items.ex: Learning to think critically is a fundamental part of any good education.

items.def: much more than is necessary, reasonable or acceptable
items.ex: Excessive screen time is often linked to poor posture and tired eyes.

items.def: enough in amount, or good enough in quality, for a particular purpose
items.ex: Many rural schools still lack adequate internet access.

items.def: a connection between two things in which one changes when the other changes
items.ex: There is a strong correlation between the time students spend practising and their exam scores.
col: a correlation between X and Y

items.def: the variety of plants and animals living in a particular area or in the world
items.ex: Large solar farms should be designed so that they do not reduce local biodiversity.

items.def: of the usual or traditional type; following accepted ways of doing things
items.ex: Electric cars are cheaper to run than conventional petrol vehicles.

items.def: happening slowly over a long period, not suddenly
items.ex: The graph shows a gradual rise in the number of women working in engineering.

items.def: to stop changing and become steady, or to make something do this
items.ex: After falling for three years, cinema attendance stabilised at around two million visits a year.

items.def: to be more than a particular number, amount or limit
items.ex: According to the projections, the number of electric cars in the city will exceed the number of petrol cars by 2035.

items.def: correct and exact, without any mistakes
items.ex: Modern sensors give far more accurate measurements of air quality than older equipment.

items.def: (of a type of animal or plant) at serious risk of no longer existing
items.ex: Drones are now used to monitor endangered species in remote forests.

items.def: to calculate what an amount or situation will be in the future, based on present information
items.ex: The number of students taking courses online is projected to double by 2040.

items.def: happening or coming after something else
items.ex: Sales rose sharply in 2019 but fell in each subsequent year.

items.def: in the end, after a long process; or when you consider the most important point
items.ex: Ultimately, it is up to parents to decide how much screen time their children have.

items.def: to find out the facts about something; or to be the main thing that controls or decides something
items.ex: Family income largely determines whether children have access to a computer at home.

items.def: to watch something carefully in order to learn about it; also, to notice something
items.ex: The researchers observed how young children interacted with robots in the classroom.

items.def: a fuel such as coal, oil or gas that formed underground from plants and animals that died millions of years ago
items.ex: Many countries still rely on fossil fuels to generate most of their electricity.

items.def: a change in position, direction or attitude
items.ex: There has been a noticeable shift from printed books to e-books among young readers.
col: a shift from X to Y

items.def: something that happens or exists and can be observed, especially something unusual or worth studying
items.ex: Working from home was once rare, but it has now become a global phenomenon.

items.def: the degree or size of something
items.ex: To some extent, technology has made workers more efficient, but it has also increased stress.

items.def: the total amount of carbon dioxide produced by the activities of a person, organisation or product
items.ex: Video conferencing can reduce a company's carbon footprint by cutting the need for business travel.

items.def: when compared with other things or with what is normal
items.ex: Online courses are relatively cheap compared with traditional university degrees.

items.def: always happening or behaving in the same way; or agreeing with other facts
items.ex: The results were consistent with earlier studies on remote learning.

items.def: to develop gradually over time; (of living things) to change slowly over many generations
items.ex: Mobile phones have evolved from simple calling devices into powerful pocket computers.

items.def: to say or believe that something is the result of a particular thing
items.ex: The researchers attributed the fall in accidents to better training for new drivers.

items.def: to happen at the same time as something else; or to be the same as something
items.ex: The rise in online shopping coincided with the spread of high-speed broadband.

items.def: to form or make up something; or to be considered as something
items.ex: According to the chart, women constituted just under a third of the engineering workforce in 2010.

items.def: to stay at the same level after a period of growth or decline; a period when this happens
items.ex: Smartphone ownership rose rapidly until 2018 and then plateaued at around 90%.
items.ar: يستقرّ عند مستوى ثابت، مرحلة ثبات

items.def: (of an amount or change) not very large
items.ex: The number of people cycling to work saw a modest increase of 3% over the period.

items.def: very small in amount or effect, and not important
items.ex: There was only a marginal increase in visitors to the museum after it introduced free Wi-Fi.

items.def: so strong or convincing that you have to accept it or pay attention to it
items.ex: There is compelling evidence that students learn better when lessons are interactive.

items.def: based on observation, measurement or experience rather than on theory alone
items.ex: Critics point out that there is little empirical evidence that brain-training apps improve memory in daily life.

items.def: to reduce the amount of something, especially a natural resource, until little is left
items.ex: Overfishing has severely depleted fish stocks in many parts of the world's oceans.

items.def: real but not immediately obvious; forming the basis of something
items.ex: Rather than simply banning phones, schools should address the underlying causes of distraction.

items.def: common or widely found in a particular place, group or period
items.ex: Short-term contracts are increasingly prevalent among recent graduates.

items.def: to make something bad less harmful, serious or painful
items.ex: Planting trees along busy roads can help to mitigate the effects of air pollution.

items.def: to make a problem or bad situation worse
items.ex: Cutting bus services would only exacerbate traffic congestion in the city centre.

items.def: a sudden and large increase; to increase suddenly and strongly
items.ex: There was a surge in demand for laptops when schools moved their lessons online.

items.def: to fall very quickly and suddenly to a much lower level
items.ex: Sales of DVDs plummeted from 40 million in 2010 to just 5 million in 2020.

items.def: very careful, thorough and exact
items.ex: Claims about new learning apps should be checked through rigorous testing before schools adopt them.

items.def: the process of something, especially the natural environment, becoming worse in quality
items.ex: Unregulated mining has led to serious degradation of farmland in the region.

items.def: to get something from a particular source
items.ex: Many students derive great satisfaction from solving difficult problems in groups.

items.def: to become, or make something, smaller, weaker or less important
items.ex: The importance of handwriting has diminished as more students type their notes.

items.def: clearly different or separate from something else; easy to notice
items.ex: There is a distinct difference between the reading habits of teenagers and those of adults.

items.def: so small that it is not important or worth considering
items.ex: The difference between the two groups' test scores was negligible.

items.def: a large difference between two or more things, especially one that seems unfair
items.ex: The chart reveals a striking disparity in internet access between urban and rural areas.
col: a disparity between X and Y

items.def: to repeat an experiment or study and get the same results
items.ex: Other research teams were unable to replicate the original findings, which cast doubt on the study.

items.def: the cutting down or burning of large areas of forest
items.ex: Deforestation not only destroys habitats but also releases large amounts of carbon dioxide.

items.def: a long period with little or no rain, causing a serious lack of water
items.ex: Farmers are using soil sensors to save water during periods of severe drought.

items.def: to gradually make something weaker or less effective
items.ex: Constant notifications can undermine students' ability to concentrate.

items.def: to make an idea, feeling or belief stronger
items.ex: Advertisements that show only men as engineers reinforce outdated stereotypes.

items.def: to make an action or process easier or more likely to happen
items.ex: Shared online documents facilitate collaboration between colleagues in different offices.

items.def: to make it difficult for something to happen or develop
items.ex: A lack of reliable internet access hinders the progress of students in remote areas.

items.def: to check or prove that something is true or correct
items.ex: Students should verify information they find online by checking more than one source.

items.def: to make something dirty or harmful by adding a dangerous substance to it
items.ex: Chemicals from discarded electronic devices can contaminate soil and groundwater.

items.def: poisonous and harmful to people, animals or the environment
items.ex: Batteries thrown away with ordinary rubbish can release toxic chemicals into the ground.

items.def: to publicly support a particular idea, policy or way of doing things; a person who does this
items.ex: Some experts advocate a complete ban on mobile phones in primary schools.

items.def: an opinion or attitude about something, especially one that is stated publicly
items.ex: In this essay, I will take the stance that technology has improved family life overall.
items.fam: no derived forms; similar: position, standpoint

items.def: general agreement among a group of people
items.ex: There is a growing consensus that children should learn basic coding from an early age.

items.def: seeming likely to be true or reasonable
items.ex: One plausible explanation for the drop in cinema attendance is the popularity of streaming services.

items.def: the way something works, or a process that produces a particular result
items.ex: Scientists still do not fully understand the mechanism by which long-term memories are formed.

items.def: impossible to change back to an earlier state
items.ex: Scientists warn that some of the damage to coral reefs may already be irreversible.
items.ar: لا رجعة فيه، لا يمكن عكسه

items.def: able to work successfully or to be done in practice
items.ex: Electric buses are now a viable alternative to diesel vehicles in most cities.

items.def: never having happened or existed before
items.ex: The past decade has seen unprecedented growth in the use of online learning platforms.

items.def: existing as a natural or basic part of something and impossible to remove
items.ex: Every new technology carries inherent risks as well as benefits.

items.def: proving that something is true and removing all doubt
items.ex: The results of the trial were far from conclusive, so the school decided to repeat it the following year.

items.def: a situation in which there is not enough of something that people need
items.ex: Water scarcity could become a major source of tension between neighbouring regions.

items.def: mostly or mainly
items.ex: The workforce in the software industry remains predominantly male.

items.def: used to introduce an idea or fact that is the opposite of the one just mentioned
items.ex: Online courses suit independent learners; conversely, students who need structure may struggle without a teacher.
col: conversely, it could be argued that

items.def: to be caused by something or develop as a result of it
items.ex: Many problems in the workplace stem from poor communication between managers and staff.

items.def: done according to a careful plan or method, step by step
items.ex: The team carried out a systematic review of forty studies on screen use and sleep.

items.def: the situation in which a type of animal or plant no longer exists
items.ex: Without stronger protection, many species of frog could face extinction within decades.

items.def: to control or limit something, especially something harmful; a limit of this kind
items.ex: Several cities have introduced congestion charges to curb car use in the centre.

items.def: a good quality or advantage; to deserve attention or a particular reaction
items.ex: Both arguments have merit, but I believe the benefits of online learning are greater.

items.def: very great or intense; having a strong and lasting effect
items.ex: The internet has had a profound impact on the way people communicate.

items.def: relating to amounts or numbers that can be measured, rather than to qualities
items.ex: The study combined quantitative data from questionnaires with in-depth interviews.

items.def: to balance the effect of something by doing something that has the opposite effect
items.ex: The airline encourages passengers to offset the emissions from their flights by funding tree planting.

items.def: having the opposite effect to the one that was intended
items.ex: Banning phones completely could be counterproductive, as students would never learn to use them responsibly.

items.def: a living thing, such as a plant, an animal or a bacterium
items.ex: Tiny organisms in the soil play an essential role in breaking down waste.

items.def: having a limit; existing only in a limited amount
items.ex: Oil and gas are finite resources, so countries need to develop alternatives now.

items.def: relating to genes, the parts of cells that pass characteristics from parents to their young
items.ex: Advances in genetic research may one day allow doctors to predict certain illnesses years in advance.

items.def: the gradual wearing away of soil or rock by wind, water or ice; also, a gradual weakening of something
items.ex: Planting grass on hillsides helps to prevent soil erosion during heavy rain.

items.def: to reach an opinion or conclusion from the information you have
items.ex: From the data, we can infer that older users adopt new apps more slowly than younger ones.

items.def: as a result of the action that has just been mentioned
items.ex: Many firms have automated routine tasks, thereby freeing staff to focus on more creative work.

items.def: although; used to add a fact that makes the previous statement less strong
items.ex: Remote learning has widened access to education, albeit at the cost of some social contact.

items.def: to state firmly that something is true, especially as part of an argument
items.ex: Some educators contend that homework does more harm than good for young children.

items.def: to admit, often unwillingly, that something is true or that the other side has a good point
items.ex: Even supporters of remote work concede that it can make teamwork more difficult.

items.def: able to be broken down naturally by bacteria into substances that do not harm the environment
items.ex: Several cafés have replaced plastic cups with biodegradable alternatives.

items.def: the process of one thing directly making another thing happen
items.ex: A correlation between screen time and low grades does not necessarily prove causation.

items.def: a substance that speeds up a chemical reaction; also, something that causes an important change to happen
items.ex: The pandemic acted as a catalyst for the rapid growth of online shopping.

items.def: to prove that a statement or argument is wrong
items.ex: The latest study refutes the claim that video games make teenagers more aggressive.

items.def: to make an action necessary or appropriate; to give a good reason for it
items.ex: The rise in online fraud warrants more security training for all employees.

items.def: to provide more evidence that supports a statement, idea or result
items.ex: Data from the second survey corroborated the earlier finding that teenagers sleep less on school nights.

items.def: to fill something up again or bring it back to its earlier level
items.ex: Underground water supplies are being used faster than rainfall can replenish them.

items.def: to slow down or block the progress of something
items.ex: Outdated regulations may impede the adoption of cleaner technologies in industry.

items.def: belonging to the basic nature of something or someone
items.ex: Students with an intrinsic interest in a subject tend to study more effectively than those motivated only by grades.

items.def: spreading widely through every part of something, often in an unwanted way
items.ex: The pervasive influence of social media on young people's opinions worries many parents and teachers.

items.def: caused or produced by human activity
items.ex: Most climate scientists agree that recent global warming is largely anthropogenic.
items.ar: بشريّ المنشأ، ناتج عن النشاط البشري

items.def: the great size or importance of something
items.ex: Few people predicted the magnitude of the changes that the internet would bring to daily life.

items.def: more important than anything else
items.ex: When designing apps for children, safety must be of paramount importance.

items.def: something unusual that is different from what is normal or expected
items.ex: The sudden drop in sales in March was an anomaly caused by a week-long power cut.

items.def: a difference between two things that should be the same or should match
items.ex: There was a clear discrepancy between what users said in the survey and how they actually behaved.

items.def: changing often and suddenly, without a regular pattern
items.ex: Visitor numbers to the website were erratic during the first year, before rising steadily.

items.def: to become gradually smaller in number or size until little remains
items.ex: The number of handwritten letters sent each year has dwindled as email and messaging apps have taken over.

items.def: to use known facts to make a judgement or prediction about a situation you do not know about
items.ex: It would be unwise to extrapolate from such a small sample to the whole population.

items.def: the process by which fertile land gradually turns into desert, often because of drought or poor farming
items.ex: Planting drought-resistant trees is one way to slow desertification in dry regions.

items.def: treating a complex issue as if it were much simpler than it really is
items.ex: It is simplistic to blame technology alone for the decline in reading among teenagers.

items.def: likely to cause disagreement or argument
items.ex: Whether robots should replace some human teachers remains a highly contentious issue.

items.def: (of carbon) to capture carbon dioxide and store it so that it does not enter the atmosphere
items.ex: Restoring wetlands is an effective way to sequester carbon naturally.

items.def: completely clear, with no doubt or uncertainty
items.ex: The committee gave its unequivocal support to the plan to provide every pupil with a laptop.

items.def: very weak or uncertain, especially about a connection or argument
items.ex: Critics argue that the link between violent video games and real-life crime is tenuous at best.

items.def: a typical model or set of ideas that explains how something works or should be done
items.ex: Online learning represents a paradigm shift in the way universities deliver their courses.

items.def: to gradually take over land, or to affect something beyond the usual or proper limits
items.ex: As cities expand, new housing developments encroach on farmland and wildlife habitats.

items.def: to produce a substance by chemical means; or to combine different ideas or pieces of information into one whole
items.ex: Strong essays synthesise ideas from several sources rather than simply listing them.

items.def: a change in the genes of a living thing that can be passed on to the next generation
items.ex: Some bacteria develop mutations that make them resistant to common antibiotics.

items.def: in its original condition; completely clean and undamaged
items.ex: Tourism can damage pristine natural areas if visitor numbers are not carefully controlled.

items.def: to suggest an idea or theory as a basis for reasoning, even though it has not been proved
items.ex: Some physicists postulate the existence of particles that have never been directly observed.
